descriptors.R: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1897, chosen with the outgoing President's backing
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1893 to 1897, renominating its candidate of 1896 and 1900

compile_desc.R: the party of the administration in office since 1897
compile_desc.D: the party that held the presidency from 1893 to 1897

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Socialist, a Prohibition, an Independence party, a People's party and a Socialist Labor nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Taft, Bryan, Sherman, Kern, Debs, Chafin, Hisgen, Watson, Roosevelt, Hearst or Cannon

slice_sources.men: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1908; men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states (including declarant aliens where they could vote); turnout and choice from the backbone, calibrated to certified 1908 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1908; women 21+ outside the South; women could vote for president only in Wyoming, Colorado (1893), Utah and Idaho (1896).
slice_sources.south-white: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1908; white adults in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults); calibrated to certified 1908 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1908; Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement was near complete across the region (Georgia's October 1908 amendment joined the poll taxes, literacy tests and grandfather clauses already in force); the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1900 and 1910 censuses interpolated to November 1908; foreign-born white adults who were aliens or had only declared their intent (first papers); declarant aliens could vote in several Midwestern and Western states (fewer each decade as states repealed it), so part of this slice could vote.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
